commons:60946201.summary: On this large silver chalice, a gilded arcade frames standing figures; here Christ, haloed and holding a book, raises his right hand in blessing beneath an arch, with a Greek inscription running around the rim above. The Met notes that the chalice carries images of Christ and the Virgin with saints and archangels, so that when it was raised at the Eucharist the congregation saw Christ's own image on the cup of his blood.
facts: Its Greek dedication asks prayers for the repose of the soul of Anastasia and the salvation of John, deacon of Saint Stephen of the village of Attarathion, according to the Met.
The cup holds about 1.5 litres, a generous size that, as the Met suggests, could be seen by a large congregation.
It is one of several chalices in the Attarouthi Treasure (Met 1986.3.5).
